title: Trie
learn: node = dict of children + end flag, insert/search/startsWith O(L), when trie beats hash set
hook: Implement Trie is a classic design question, and tries are what make Word Search II and autocomplete feasible. Any time the word "prefix" appears in a problem, a trie should come to mind.

explain.prompt: Explain what a trie is, how insert, search and startsWith work, and when you'd use one instead of a hash set.
keyPoints: each node holds children keyed by character plus an end-of-word flag
insert walks/creates one node per character and marks the last node as a word end
search walks the path and requires the end flag; startsWith only requires the path to exist
all operations are O(L) for a word of length L, independent of how many words are stored
a hash set answers exact lookups but can't answer prefix queries without scanning every word
